title: Delete using prev
summary: The node already knows its neighbour on each side, so no search is needed.

checkpoints.text: `doomed` points at the middle node, 20. In a singly linked list we would now have to walk from `head` to find the node before it. Here, `prev` already says it is 10.
10 now points forward at 30. 20 is unlinked in both directions, but it still exists in memory.
20 is freed. `doomed` in `main` still holds its old address: it is now a dangling pointer and must not be used.
Deleting the first node: `head` has to move to the next node, or it would be left pointing at freed memory.
Only 30 is left. One function handled both the middle node and the first node.
